info.name: backend-concepts
info.description:
Express learning API: admin products + users, shop (published), cart (logged-in users only), and auth (signup/login).

Run server: yarn start → [http://localhost:3040](http://localhost:3040)

Body: raw JSON. Use the Local env or the collection variable `baseUrl`.

Auth: login returns a JWT (`data.accessToken`, 15 minutes); the Login request saves it to the `token` variable. `GET /auth/me` requires `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}`. `/admin` (the Admin and User folders) requires an **admin** token: those folders use Bearer `{{token}}`. 401 without/with a bad token, 403 `"Admins only"` for a customer token. The first admin is created by SQL.

Cart: logged-in users only. The Cart folder uses Bearer `{{token}}` (run Login first); no token or a bad one → 401. A customer token is enough. Each user has one cart (`carts.userId`) plus `cart_items`. GET/POST/DELETE `/cart` return items with `cartId`, `productId`, `quantity`, and a nested `product`. Add/remove body is `{ productId }` (published products only).

Validation: every request body is checked by a zod schema before the controller. A bad body → 400 `{ message: "Invalid body", errors: { field: [...] } }` listing every bad field; unknown fields are dropped. Rules that need the database stay in the services (404 / 409). The "→ 400" requests show examples.

User responses never include `password`.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Admin product routes under `/admin`. Requires an admin token (Bearer `{{token}}`, inherited by every request here): 401 no/bad token, 403 not admin.

request.description: 201 with the new product (`imageUrl` is `null` until an image is uploaded with "Upload product image"). Body is validated first: `title` 1–255 chars, `price` number ≥ 0, `description` non-empty, `isPublished` boolean. A bad body → 400 listing every bad field. Unknown fields (e.g. `id`, `imageUrl`) are dropped. Sets `productId` on success.

Example of validation: expect 400 `{ message: "Invalid body", errors: { title, price, description, isPublished } }`. Every bad field is listed at once; `role` is not an error, it is simply dropped. Needs an admin token like the rest of this folder.

Full replace (id in the URL). Same body rules as Add product (400 lists every bad field). Does not change the image (`imageUrl` is dropped); use "Upload product image". 400 if the id is not a positive integer, 404 if the product does not exist.

multipart/form-data with one field `image` (type **File**). Pick the file in Body → form-data before sending. Only `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, max 2 MB. The server picks the file name and saves `/images/<file>` in `imageUrl`; open `{{baseUrl}}/images/<file>` to see it.

200 with the product. 400 no file or wrong type, 413 too big, 400 bad id, 404 product not found (the uploaded file is removed). A new image replaces the old one, and the old file is deleted.

Don't set Content-Type yourself: Postman adds it with the boundary.
400 if the id is not a positive integer. 404 if the product does not exist. Also deletes the product's uploaded image file (if it has one).

item.name: Cart
item.description: Cart for the logged-in user. Every request needs `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` (set on this folder; run **Auth → Login** first). No token, or a malformed, invalid, or expired one → **401** (sign up or log in first). A customer token is enough. Responses are the item list: `id`, `cartId`, `productId`, `quantity`, and a nested `product`.

request.description: Items in the logged-in user's cart (an empty cart is created on the first call). `data` is `[{ id, cartId, productId, quantity, product }]`. 401 without a valid token.

Your own cart as a PDF (`Content-Type: application/pdf`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="quote.pdf"`). To save the file: click the arrow next to **Send** → **Download response**. The PDF is streamed and not saved on the server.

200 with the PDF. 400 `"Cart is empty"` if the cart has no items. 401 without a token. The cart comes from the token, so you can only get your own.

Add one unit of a published product. Repeat to increment quantity. `productId` must be a positive whole number (a JSON number, not "6") → else 400. 404 if the product does not exist or is unpublished. Returns the full item list.
Example of validation: "abc" is the wrong shape → 400 from the schema, before the service runs. Compare with a well-formed id that doesn't exist (e.g. 99999) → 404 from the service.
Subtract one unit. Drops the line at 0. 400 if `productId` is not a positive whole number.
Empty the logged-in user's cart (deletes its items; the cart row stays).

item.name: User
item.description: Admin user management under `/admin`. Requires an admin token (Bearer `{{token}}`, inherited by every request here): 401 no/bad token, 403 not admin. Responses never include `password`.

request.description: 404 if the user does not exist.

Body rules: valid `email`, `password` 8–72 chars, `firstName` / `lastName` 1–100 chars. `role` is optional: `customer` (default) or `admin`; anything else → 400. A bad body → 400 listing every bad field. 409 if the email already exists. Sets `userId` on success.
Full replace: same body rules as Add user (no `role`; if sent it is dropped, the role never changes). Password is re-hashed. 404 if the user does not exist, 409 if the email belongs to another user.
400 if the id is not a positive integer. 404 if the user does not exist.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Users acting for themselves. Login returns a JWT access token and saves it to `token`; `GET /auth/me` sends it as `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}`.

request.description: 201 with the new user (always `customer`; a `role` in the body is dropped). Body rules: valid `email`, `password` 8–72 chars, `firstName` / `lastName` 1–100 chars. A bad body → 400 listing every bad field. 409 if the email already exists.
Example of validation: expect 400 with `errors.email`, `errors.password` (8–72 chars) and `errors.firstName` (blank after trim).

200 with `data.accessToken` (JWT, 15 minutes). Sets `token` on success. 400 only if email or password is missing (no password rules here, so older accounts with short passwords like `test123` still work). 401 "Invalid email or password" for a wrong email or wrong password.
The caller's own user, from the token (run Login first). 401 if the header is missing/malformed or the token is invalid or expired. 404 if the user was deleted after the token was issued.
